chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who has some dirhams for me, so I go to him and say, 'Exchange them for dinars without me taking possession of anything.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.' I said, 'There are dinars for me, so I go to him and say, 'Exchange them for me into dirhams and keep them established with you,' and I do not take anything from him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to exchange gold for silver without taking physical possession immediately?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the flexibility of the possession (qabd) condition in spot currency exchange (sarf) when conducted via book-entry or accounting records rather than physical handover. It reflects the practical needs of early Islamic commerce, where scholars like Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permitted the transfer of value through established accounts, ensuring the transaction remains a spot exchange (bay' al-sarf) without falling into riba. This view supports the permissibility of modern banking mechanisms where funds are transferred electronically without immediate physical cash handling.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man happened to have some Dirhams with him, for me. So I went over to him and I said, ‘Change these Dinars without me having taken possession of anything’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’. I said, ‘There happens to be Dinars for me, so I go over to him and said, ‘Change these for me into Dirhams and keep these established with you’, and I do not take anything from it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 12. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il from Mansur ibn Yunus from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man with whom I had a certain amount of dinars; I asked him to change them to dirhams and keep them with himself. I did not take possession of any of them . 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful . 555
